comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the temporal characterization of s-LNv axon projection development (C2, C3, C13-C16). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements and statistical analysis, while peer reviewers note 'solid methodology' and 'well done experiments.' OpenEval additionally includes C77 (growth cone pausing) which peer reviewers address separately in R7.

Perfect agreement on claims C4, C17, C22-C25, C69 regarding MB calyx growth correlation with s-LNv vertical projection. Both evaluations accept the correlation analysis and ablation experiments as strong evidence. OpenEval highlights specific correlation coefficients and p-values, while peer reviewers acknowledge the ablation findings without methodological critique.

Complete alignment on Dscam1's cell-autonomous role in horizontal projection (C5, C26-C32, C34-C36). Both evaluations accept the RNAi, mutant analysis, and specificity for horizontal projection. OpenEval details the complementary experimental approaches, while peer reviewers explicitly state they accept the Dscam1 mechanism as part of the directional change mechanism.

Full concordance on Netrin-Dscam1 signaling mechanism (C39-C44, C72-C73, C76). Both evaluations support the genetic redundancy between NetA and NetB, and the neuronal source of Netrins. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly accepts the Netrin-mediated repulsion mechanism, while OpenEval emphasizes the tissue-specific manipulation evidence.

Both evaluations support DN-specific Netrin signaling (C45-C50, C79-C80 in OpenEval; C45-C50 in peer review). OpenEval focuses on cell-type-specific manipulations and temporal ablation, while peer reviewers explicitly note DNs' active role in s-LNv morphology. Peer review R5 also includes temporal correlation claims (C51-C58, C81) that OpenEval addresses in R6.

Substantial overlap on temporal correlation between DN birth and axon directional change (C51-C58, C81). OpenEval R6 addresses C6-C7, C51-C58, C62, C81 with emphasis on quantitative cell counting and NetB expression timing. Peer R5 accepts these temporal findings as part of the DN-Netrin mechanism. OpenEval notes the causal relationship relies on inference from combined evidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C61, C75) regarding ectopic Netrin expression disrupting horizontal projection. Both evaluations support these gain-of-function experiments. OpenEval explicitly describes the misexpression experiments, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of the overall experimental suite without specific critique.

Partial overlap on growth cone pausing (C77, C78). OpenEval R8 addresses C77-C78 and C85 as interpretive conclusions requiring integration of multiple evidence lines. Peer R7 implicitly accepts C77-C78 as part of the developmental trajectory without explicit discussion, encompassed in their acceptance of 'solid methodology' for axonal growth studies.

Both address the integrative conclusion about the directional change mechanism (C85). OpenEval characterizes this as an inference from collective findings about intermediate targets and waiting mechanisms. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the novelty of the mechanism and state experiments are 'conclusive,' providing stronger endorsement of the integrative interpretation.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty regarding DN3 identity (C84). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers classify this as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes the lack of cell-specific labeling tools, and peer reviewers do not validate or challenge the specific DN3 identification, accepting the authors' acknowledgment of speculation.

OpenEval R10 addresses 24 background knowledge claims (C1, C8-C11, C18-C21, C33, C37-C38, C59-C60, C63-C67, C70-C71, C74, C82-C83) supported by literature citations. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these contextual/background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval R11 addresses methodological validation of the Pdf-GAL4 driver (C12) with immunostaining data. Peer reviewers do not explicitly comment on this technical validation, though their acceptance of the overall methodology implicitly encompasses this foundational control.

Minimal direct overlap (only C62) but thematically related. OpenEval R6 focuses on temporal correlation and NetB expression patterns, while peer R6 addresses the broader integrative conclusion about the directional change mechanism (C62, C85). Both support their respective claims but at different levels of interpretation.
